job.title: Project Manager – HV Infrastructure
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

About the role

The Project Manager – HV Infrastructure supports the delivery of high-voltage infrastructure for STACK's data centre developments across Australia, managing assigned project packages and coordinating contractors, engineering and delivery interfaces. The role manages assigned HV works from design and procurement through construction, testing, commissioning and energisation. Projects may include substations, transformers, switchgear, HV cables/lines, contestable works, BESS and associated infrastructure. The Project Manager coordinates day-to-day delivery with HV EPC contractors and works closely with the Project Director - HV Infrastructure, Grid Connection Manager, DC Engineering, DC Delivery and network service providers.

Key responsibilities

  • Manage assigned HV infrastructure projects or work packages from ECI and design through EPC execution, commissioning and energisation
  • Maintain detailed project schedules and track engineering, procurement, long-lead equipment, construction, testing and energisation milestones
  • Track and manage assigned scope, programme, cost, risk, quality and changes, escalating matters outside delegated authority
  • Coordinate delivery of substations, contestable works, HV cables/lines, transformers, switchgear, BESS and associated infrastructure as applicable
  • Support procurement and manage the day-to-day performance of HV EPC contractors and specialist delivery partners
  • Monitor EPC performance against programme, cost, quality and contractual obligations
  • Work closely with the Principal Engineer – HV Infrastructure to ensure technical requirements are incorporated into EPC design and delivery
  • Coordinate the testing, commissioning and energisation programme for assigned HV works
  • Promote a strong safety culture across all HV project activities
  • Prepare clear project reporting on programme, cost, risk and delivery status for project leadership

About you

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management or related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience
  • 5–8 years' relevant experience in electrical, transmission, renewable-energy, utility or infrastructure projects
  • Experience supporting delivery of HV substations or associated electrical infrastructure
  • Experience managing contractors or defined construction packages
  • Experience across several project phases, including engineering, procurement, construction or commissioning
  • Strong understanding of project controls, programme, cost, risk and contract management
  • Sound project management skills in electrical or infrastructure delivery
  • Strong knowledge of HV electrical infrastructure and substation delivery
  • Strong programme, commercial, risk and change-management capability
  • Strong stakeholder management, negotiation and communication skills

Equal Opportunity Employer

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

job.title: Project Engineer – HV Infrastructure
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

About the role

The Project Engineer – HV Infrastructure is a technically focused project delivery role within STACK's Power & Energy function, responsible for managing engineering workstreams and resolving technical issues across high-voltage infrastructure projects from design through construction, commissioning and energisation. The role takes ownership of assigned technical deliverables and interfaces, coordinating EPC contractors, consultants and OEMs to achieve timely engineering decisions and maintain delivery progress. It works closely with HV Project Managers, the Grid Connection Manager and the DC Engineering team. The role covers HV substations, transformers, switchgear, cables, protection and control, BESS and associated infrastructure, with a strong focus on design coordination, technical change management, equipment integration and construction readiness.

Key responsibilities

  • Own assigned HV engineering workstreams, technical action plans and deliverable schedules; proactively identify issues affecting construction or commissioning.
  • Investigate technical queries, design clashes, non-conformances and equipment interface issues; coordinate practical solutions with EPC contractors, consultants and OEMs.
  • Review technical drawings, specifications, equipment data and design submissions for completeness, consistency and alignment with approved requirements.
  • Lead technical coordination meetings and site issue-resolution sessions; assign actions, manage dependencies and drive timely closure.
  • Manage the technical review process for assigned EPC deliverables, RFIs, equipment submissions and engineering documentation, including consolidated comments and closeout.
  • Drive design workshops, constructability reviews and interface coordination between HV EPC, OEMs, consultants and data centre teams.
  • Maintain technical change registers and assess programme, procurement and construction impacts of proposed design changes before escalation.
  • Lead technical issue resolution for assigned HV packages during construction, installation, testing and energisation, supporting HV Project Managers and EPC contractors.
  • Plan and coordinate technical participation in FATs, SATs, site inspections and commissioning reviews; track technical punch-list closeout.
  • Own technical issue, design change, RFI, interface and engineering deliverable registers for assigned workstreams.

About you

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline.
  • 5+ years' relevant experience in HV engineering, substations, utilities, renewable energy or major electrical infrastructure projects.
  • Demonstrated experience managing engineering deliverables and technical interfaces during design, construction or commissioning of HV assets.
  • Experience coordinating EPC contractors, engineering consultants and OEMs to resolve technical issues and manage design changes.
  • Working knowledge of Australian electrical standards and relevant safety requirements.
  • Experience owning technical workstreams, engineering registers, technical queries and construction interface resolution.
  • Strong practical knowledge of HV substations and the technical delivery of electrical infrastructure.
  • Ability to interpret single-line diagrams, equipment drawings, specifications and technical reports.
  • Working knowledge of transformers, switchgear, HV cables, protection and control and associated systems.
  • Ability to independently investigate technical issues, coordinate specialist inputs and drive solutions through to closure.

job.title: Assistant Manage - Environment, Health & Safety
job.description:
Responsibilities

Facility Inspections and Risk Identification:

  • Conduct thorough inspections to identify safety, health, and environmental risks and develop and implement inspection policies, procedures, and schedules.

Health and Safety Procedures:

  • Develop and enforce health and safety procedures across all areas of the company and review and update emergency procedures and workplace safety protocols.

Training and Compliance:

  • Prepare and deliver training on emergency procedures, workplace safety, and chemical safety and monitor compliance with training requirements and conduct periodic training sessions.

Monitoring and Enforcement:

  • Monitor critical activities on-site and correct unsafe practices through a stop-the-line approach and implement and monitor the Permit to Work system effectively.

Inspections and Audits:

  • Carry out daily inspections and audits of EHS observations, maintaining a comprehensive list of action items and review the effectiveness of general ventilation and Local Exhaust Ventilation (LEV) systems through regular measurement and monitoring.

Incident Reporting and Investigation:

  • Lead near-miss reporting and investigations to prevent major accidents and incidents and develop and implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) based on investigation findings.

Training Program Development:

  • Develop and deliver training programs on process safety management, toxicology, ergonomics, and other critical EHS subjects and ensure training programs align with regulatory requirements and company standards.

Promotion of EHS Awareness:

  • Actively lead initiatives to celebrate various EHS awareness days and weeks among employees and contractors and promote a strong safety culture and adherence to EHS guidelines throughout the solar manufacturing facility.

job.title: MCIM Engineer
job.description:
Who we are

Where performance meets sustainability, Digital Edge is a leading data center platform in Asia Pacific, delivering sustainable, next-generation, AI-ready digital infrastructure at scale. Headquartered in Singapore and backed by Stonepeak, we operate a rapidly expanding platform with over 30 data centers and 1.8GW of secured IT power across key markets.

Our mission is to build the foundation for the world’s digital future, helping organizations to grow sustainably and empowering the populations they serve. We differentiate through execution – delivering at speed and at scale while combining global standards with deep local expertise. This enables us to provide consistent, sustainable and high-performance infrastructure for hyperscalers and enterprises across the region.

As Asia Pacific’s digital transformation accelerates, Digital Edge is building the infrastructure that powers the next wave of AI and cloud growth. Joining Digital Edge means being part of a high-growth platform at the forefront of AI and cloud infrastructure, where you can make a tangible impact on Asia-Pacific’s digital future.

Our values:

  • Respect: We embrace diversity and collaboration.
  • Innovation: We share ideas and solve problems.
  • Strive: We are driven and determined.
  • Excellence: We seek to deliver the best.
  • Responsibility: We do what’s right for our people and the planet.

What we need:

The MCIM Engineer is accountable for country and site-level administration, data integrity, workflow compliance and operational adoption of the Mission Critical Infrastructure Management platform across assigned data center facilities. Reporting directly to the in-country Manager, Operations Support, with a dotted-line reporting relationship to the platform Director, MCIM and Asset Management, the role ensures critical assets, maintenance activities, incidents, operational changes, corrective actions and supporting evidence are accurately managed through MCIM as the authoritative operational system of record.

The role acts as the primary interface between Facility Operations and the central MCIM Platform team, translating platform standards, asset taxonomies, workflows and governance requirements into disciplined country and site-level execution. The MCIM Engineer supports users, monitors compliance, validates operational data, coordinates system improvements and ensures activities undertaken by employees, contractors and service providers are complete, traceable and audit-ready.

The Director, MCIM and Asset Management owns platform strategy, system standards, core workflow design, configuration governance, asset taxonomy and cross-country standardization. The in-country Manager, Operations Support owns local leadership, prioritization and integration of MCIM requirements into country operations. Facility Operations remains accountable for the safe and correct execution of operational work. The MCIM Engineer does not replace these accountabilities but ensures the work is properly planned, controlled, recorded and evidenced through the platform.

Key responsibilities

  • Own country and site-level MCIM administration, adoption, data integrity and workflow compliance across assigned data center facilities, ensuring the platform is consistently used for applicable asset, maintenance, incident, change, corrective-action and operational activities.
  • Maintain complete and accurate critical infrastructure asset records, including asset classifications, hierarchies, technical attributes, equipment relationships, dependencies, maintenance requirements, lifecycle status and supporting documentation.
  • Coordinate asset-data preparation, validation, migration and reconciliation during new facility delivery, commissioning, operational readiness, expansion, retrofit, equipment replacement and decommissioning activities.
  • Administer preventive, predictive and corrective maintenance workflows within MCIM, ensuring work orders are properly planned, authorized, assigned, executed, evidenced, reviewed and closed in accordance with approved maintenance strategies and operating requirements.
  • Govern site-level incident, root cause and corrective-action records, ensuring events are correctly classified, escalated and linked to affected assets, with complete evidence and timely investigation, verification and closure of corrective and preventive actions.
  • Administer operational change workflows, verifying that changes include the required scope, risk assessment, technical and operational review, authorization, implementation planning, asset linkage, communications, execution evidence and post-implementation validation.
  • Monitor data quality and workflow performance, identifying incomplete records, untracked activities, duplicated data, configuration inconsistencies, control gaps and deviations from approved platform standards, and coordinating timely corrective action.
  • Support MCIM implementation, configuration, enhancement, upgrade, integration, pilot and user acceptance testing activities, documenting operational requirements and validating that workflows and system outputs are effective for live data center operations.
  • Develop operational dashboards and recurring reports, provide user training and first-line process support, and support internal and customer audits through accurate records, traceable workflows, complete evidence and timely remediation of identified gaps.

Actively champion and implement the organization’s policies on health & safety, environment, energy, quality, information security, and business continuity, ensuring adherence to incident reporting, legal, and regulatory requirements.

The successful candidate:

  • Relevant experience in data center operations, critical facilities, infrastructure asset management, maintenance planning, operational systems administration or a comparable mission-critical or high-availability environment.
  • Relevant degree, diploma or professional qualification in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, building services engineering, facilities management, information systems, asset management or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Practical experience using or administering CMMS, DCIM, EAM, work-order management, asset-management, maintenance-management or comparable operational platforms.
  • Strong working knowledge of asset lifecycle management, preventive and corrective maintenance, incident management, change control, operational risk assessment, corrective-action management and audit evidence requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience maintaining accurate asset and operational data, resolving data-quality issues and record inconsistencies, and producing reliable operational reports and dashboards.
  • Experience supporting system implementation, workflow configuration, data migration, platform enhancement, user acceptance testing or the integration of operational technology and enterprise systems.
  • Sound understanding of data center critical infrastructure, including electrical, mechanical, controls, monitoring, life-safety and associated building systems.
  • Proven ability to work across Facility Operations, Engineering Operations, digital platform teams, project teams, contractors, vendors and service providers, supported by strong analytical, organizational, documentation and problem-solving capability.
  • Must have strong English-language verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to deliver user training, prepare high-quality operational reports, communicate compliance requirements and engage technical and senior stakeholders; familiarity with applicable asset management, quality, information security, business continuity, safety, environmental and ISO management systems is advantageous.

Join us to shape the future of Digital Infrastructure in Asia. Apply now for a confidential career discussion.

  • Strong understanding of contractor Health and Safety governance, including prequalification, mobilisation, competency, high-risk activity planning, performance management, and assurance.
  • Experience developing and implementing technical Health and Safety standards, assurance frameworks, leading indicators, competency frameworks, training programs, and portfolio-level programs.

  • Proven ability to influence senior Construction, Design & Engineering, Commissioning, contractor, and country leadership stakeholders and embed Health and Safety into project planning and decision-making.
  • Strong knowledge of international Health and Safety standards, risk management principles, and relevant regulatory requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide Health and Safety leadership across multiple projects, countries, and differing construction risk environments, with regular travel across the region.

job.title: Principal Network Architect
job.description:
SG

Company: Digital Edge DC

Who we are

Digital Edge is a trusted and forward-looking data centre platform company, established to transform digital infrastructure in Asia. Backed by Stonepeak, a leading alternative investment firm specialising in infrastructure and real assets, Digital Edge has in excess of US$1 billion in committed capital.

Our mission is to bridge the digital divide across Asia Pacific by building the sustainable digital ecosystems of the future. Through building and operating state-of-the-art, energy efficient data centres rich with connectivity options, we bring new colocation and interconnect options to the Asian market, making digital infrastructure deployment in the region easy, efficient and economical.

Founded in 2020 the company has grown rapidly across multiple markets in the region, and currently provides data centre and fibre services across China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, and the Philippines. This role is an exciting opportunity to join our fast growing team as we further expand our footprint across Asia.

Our Values:

  • Responsibility: We take ownership of our actions and outcomes.
  • Innovation: We embrace change and create bold solutions.
  • Strive: We show grit, resilience and relentless drive.
  • Excellence: We pursue the highest standards in all we do.
  • Respect: We act with integrity and treat others with dignity.

What we need:

Reporting to the Director of Digital Infrastructure Operations, the Principal Network Architect owns the end-to-end network architecture across Digital Edge’s WAN, backbone, data centre, interconnection and hybrid cloud environments. The role combines deep network expertise with a practical understanding of compute, operating systems, virtualisation, storage and application dependencies to deliver high-performance, resilient services.

The architect will translate business and workload requirements into integrated designs, evaluate trade-offs across infrastructure domains, and lead delivery with systems, platform, security and application teams. Success is measured by end-to-end service performance, availability, recoverability, operational efficiency and lifecycle cost.

Key responsibilities

1. Holistic Infrastructure Architecture

  • Own integrated architecture, reference designs, and roadmaps connecting physical and optical infrastructure, IP networks, compute, storage, and platforms.
  • Map application flows and service dependencies; define capacity, latency, availability, security, recovery, and lifecycle cost requirements.
  • Document design trade-offs, migration plans, acceptance criteria and operational ownership for each architecture decision.
  • Establish and govern network architecture standards, design principles and an architecture review process, ensuring new builds and expansions across the regional portfolio conform to approved designs.
  • Develop CapEx and OpEx business cases, total cost of ownership models and multi-year network budgets to support new data centre builds and capacity expansion.

2. Systems and Platform Design Considerations

  • Apply a working understanding of Linux, server hardware, CPU and memory resources, virtualisation, and containers to network design decisions; hands-on engineering of these platforms remains with the systems and platform teams.
  • Assess how host networking, TCP/IP behaviour, NICs, MTU, virtual switches, load balancers, DNS, and time synchronisation affect service delivery.
  • Account for storage access, I/O performance, replication, clustering, and backup traffic when designing bandwidth, latency, and recovery requirements.
  • Engage systems and application specialists during design to understand host, storage, and service dependencies, and review workload test results to confirm network designs meet performance requirements.

3. Network Service Architecture and Technology Selection

  • Architect WAN, backbone, data centre, internet and cloud connectivity as an integrated end-to-end design across sites, carriers and markets, supporting both IPv4 and IPv6.
  • Select the appropriate routing, switching, overlay and transport technologies for each service type, such as internal infrastructure, customer interconnection, data centre interconnect and cloud connectivity, based on scale, resilience, latency, security, operational complexity and cost.
  • Define routing and traffic-control architecture principles, including domain hierarchy, policy, segmentation, traffic engineering and convergence, proving each principle with working reference configurations before engineering teams complete detailed design and rollout.
  • Maintain a technology selection framework and service design patterns that map service requirements to approved technologies, reviewing them as technologies and business needs evolve.
  • Architect customer interconnection services, including cross-connects, internet exchange, IP transit and cloud on-ramps, and support sales and solutions teams with customer-facing technical design and pre-sales engagement.

4. Physical Infrastructure and Optical Transport

  • Define cabling and physical infrastructure standards, including patching, labelling, route diversity and acceptance testing, ensuring the physical design supports the resilience and capacity needs of each service.
  • Select the appropriate optical transport approach for each service type, such as dark fibre, DWDM or managed wavelength services, based on capacity, reach, latency, protection and cost.
  • Validate optical and physical designs through link budget validation, transceiver interoperability and acceptance testing before handover to engineering for build and rollout.

5. Service Performance and Resilience

  • Engineer high throughput and predictable latency, jitter, and packet loss through capacity planning, QoS, traffic engineering, and system tuning.
  • Align network redundancy and convergence with host clustering, application failover, storage replication, and recovery time and recovery point objectives.
  • Design failure domains and diverse paths; validate service behaviour during peak load, maintenance, and link, device, host, or site failures.
  • Define service-level indicators and objectives, telemetry, and performance baselines spanning network and systems components.
  • Architect network security controls in partnership with the security team, including segmentation, zero-trust access, firewalling, DDoS mitigation, MACsec and IPsec encryption, and secure management-plane design.

6. Technical Leadership and Delivery

  • Lead design reviews, proofs of concept, migrations, and production readiness across infrastructure, platform, security, and application teams.
  • Produce reference configuration snippets for each design and prove them in a lab or proof-of-concept environment on target platforms, demonstrating the design is workable and operational before handover to engineering for full build and rollout.
  • Guide complex fault isolation across physical, optical, network, operating system, and platform layers, working with domain specialists.
  • Mentor engineers, maintain clear design and operational documentation, and explain architectural decisions to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Act as the senior technical escalation point for complex or major network incidents, participating in on-call escalation as required, and lead post-incident reviews that identify systemic and architectural root causes, resolving them through corrections to reference designs, standards and permanent corrective actions.

7. Automation and AI Operations

  • Champion network automation and NetDevOps practices, including infrastructure as code using Terraform and Ansible, a network source of truth, CI/CD pipelines for configuration changes, pre-change validation and streaming telemetry, driving configuration consistency and lifecycle management across the estate.
  • Define the architecture and governance for AI-assisted network operations, including AI agents connected to network automation, telemetry and source-of-truth platforms through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), with guardrails such as read-only defaults, human approval for changes, role-based access and audit logging.

8. Vendor and Commercial Management

  • Own the Request for Proposal (RFP) process with OEMs and partners, defining technical requirements, evaluation criteria and scoring models to give full visibility of competing solutions and a like-for-like technical and commercial comparison.
  • Shape vendor and carrier strategy, providing input to commercial negotiations and managing strategic OEM, partner and carrier relationships.

The successful candidate:

  • 15+ years of network engineering experience, including at least 7 years in an architecture role, delivering large-scale WAN and backbone architecture, with demonstrated systems knowledge and cross-domain solution ownership.
  • Expert knowledge of routing, switching, overlay and transport technologies, such as BGP, IS-IS, OSPF, MPLS, Segment Routing and EVPN-VXLAN, with the judgement to select the right technology for each service type.
  • Strong expertise in physical cabling, DWDM, optical technologies, and integration of optical transport with IP networks.
  • Working understanding of Linux, compute infrastructure, virtualisation, storage concepts, and application connectivity dependencies, sufficient to inform network design decisions.
  • Hands-on configuration and lab validation skills across major network operating systems, such as Cisco IOS XR and NX-OS, Juniper Junos and Arista EOS, with the ability to build and test working reference configurations.
  • Hands-on experience with network automation and infrastructure as code, including Terraform, Ansible and Python, together with version control and CI/CD workflows.
  • Ability to diagnose service performance using host metrics, logs, packet analysis, and network telemetry, and distinguish network from system constraints.
  • Proven delivery of holistic solutions balancing workload needs, security, resilience, capacity, operational complexity, and cost.
  • Working knowledge of network security architecture and compliance frameworks such as ISO 27001, SOC 2 and PCI DSS, and of data centre and telecommunications regulatory requirements across Asia Pacific markets.
  • Experience developing business cases, budgets, vendor evaluations and RFPs, including technical and commercial comparison of OEM and partner proposals, and presenting architectural recommendations to senior leadership and customers.
  • Experience working across multiple countries in Asia Pacific, with willingness to travel regionally as required.
  • Strong technical leadership and stakeholder management; a relevant degree or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred (advantageous):

  • Network design and architecture certifications such as Cisco Certified Design Expert (CCDE) or Cisco Certified Architect (CCAr).
  • CCIE, JNCIE, or equivalent advanced expertise, complemented by systems, cloud, or platform engineering experience.
  • Experience with SRv6, Segment Routing traffic engineering, coherent optical backbones, and disaster recovery exercises.
  • Experience with AI-assisted network operations (AIOps), including large language model agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations with network tooling.

Success measures:

  • Designs are handed to engineering with validated reference configurations, with minimal rework needed during implementation.
  • Integrated solutions meet agreed service availability, response time, throughput, capacity, and recovery objectives.
  • Workloads sustain planned growth and defined failures; migrations and maintenance meet service continuity targets.
  • Cross-domain design and automation reduce bottlenecks, recurring incidents, recovery effort, and lifecycle cost.

  • Accommodate pre-planned travel as required for the role

Minimum Qualifications

  • Experience in subsea cables, fiber infrastructure, and carrier market players, and familiarity with evolving commercial trends

job.title: AI Research Scientist
job.description:
Meta's Fundamental AI Research lab is seeking a Research Scientist to drive foundational research aimed at advancing physical AI capabilities. We seek to generate advanced engineer designs such as robotic hardware, mobile vehicles, and novel semiconductors. This role will involve heavy software research engineering, such large-scale data manipulation and simulator integration.

Responsibilities

  • Explore and develop novel post-training paradigms for LLMs using reinforcement learning
  • Explore and develop novel LLM post-training recipes using 3D data
  • Integrate large-scale simulation into LLM post-training
  • Explore mechanical, aerospace, civil, and other engineering disciplines and how to enable LLMs to solve key problems in these domains

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Degree must be completed prior to joining Meta
  • Currently has or is in the process of obtaining a PhD degree in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Vision (3D), Physical AI, Machine Learning, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Degree must be completed prior to joining Meta
  • Research experience in at least one of the following research areas: reinforcement learning, representation learning, self-supervised learning, multimodal learning, robotics policy development, computer vision (3D), egocentric perception, embodied AI and/or LLMs, control theory, optimization algorithms
  • Experience in C/C++ and Python and deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proven track record of achieving significant results as demonstrated by grants, fellowships, patents, as well as first-authored publications at leading workshops or conferences such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, JMLR and Computer Vision (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, TPAMI)
  • This position will require knowledge of post-training for LLMs using reinforcement learning techniques. It will also involve novel modalities such as 3D and engineering domain-specific simulators, so computer vision expertise in 3D is welcome as well
  • Experience integrating and debugging prototype/scientific software-hardware systems including mechanical, aerospace, or civil engineering domain-specific simulation
  • Experience working and communicating cross-functionally in a team environment
  • Prior work experience in the fields of mechanical, aerospace, civil engineering or other engineering domains

job.title: Product Design Technician - Level II - OFFC
job.description:
Job Summary

The Product Design Technician – Level II creates and maintains engineering specifications for Cummins products, including 3D CAD models, assemblies, and production drawings. The role ensures that product specifications meet Cummins, industry, national, and international standards while maintaining high levels of design quality, accuracy, and configuration control.

The role supports the development and maintenance of EBU component and assembly designs , works closely with engineers and cross-functional teams, and contributes to engineering change activities, drawing quality reviews, and continuous improvement. The position requires intermediate-level technical knowledge, strong attention to detail, and the ability to progressively take ownership of assigned design and drafting activities.

Key Responsibilities

CAD Modeling & Design

  • Create, modify, and maintain 3D component and assembly models using Creo based on engineering requirements, design inputs, packaging constraints, and applicable standards.
  • Support engineers in developing CAD concepts and basic design solutions for assigned EBU components and assemblies.
  • Apply mechanical design principles to develop accurate and practical design concepts that meet product and customer requirements.
  • Escalate complex design or technical decisions to the responsible engineer or technical lead.

Engineering Drawings & Specifications

  • Create and revise production engineering drawings using Creo , including dimensions, tolerances, GD&T, notes, material information, and other required specifications.
  • Develop complete product specifications through solid models, configured engineering BOMs, and detailed drawings that communicate design intent for manufacturing and inspection.
  • Apply Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) appropriately to product specifications.
  • Ensure models and drawings meet applicable Cummins, industry, national, and international standards.
  • Participate in Drawing Quality Reviews and incorporate feedback to improve design and documentation quality.

CAD Quality & Configuration Management

  • Perform detailed self-checks of Creo models and drawings before formal review, including geometry, dimensions, interfaces, clearances, drawing details, and design requirements.
  • Use Windchill and CAD data management tools to manage models, drawings, revisions, product data, and lifecycle activities.
  • Maintain accurate product configuration and ensure appropriate control and traceability of engineering data.
  • Implement approved engineering changes through CR/CN/CA processes , updating Creo models, drawings, revisions, and associated Windchill information.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Process internal engineering work requests and deliver assigned activities within agreed quality and timing expectations.
  • Engage with engineering, manufacturing, quality, product, and other functional teams as required.
  • Obtain and incorporate relevant technical inputs into models, drawings, and product specifications.
  • Communicate technical issues, risks, and potential delays proactively.

Product Knowledge & Continuous Development

  • Develop working knowledge of EBU products, mechanical components, interfaces, manufacturing processes, GD&T, and applicable engineering/design standards .
  • Consider manufacturing and lifecycle requirements when developing product specifications and design documentation.
  • Learn from drawing reviews, checker feedback, quality issues, and completed assignments and apply those learnings to future work.
  • Progressively take greater ownership of assigned work and require less supervision as technical capability develops.
  • Participate in maintaining standards, practices, and processes that support consistent engineering quality.

Core Competencies

Technical Competencies

  • Mechanical Design Modeling and Analysis – Creates CAD models in accordance with Cummins standards to represent product and system design concepts and support engineering analysis such as dimensional variation analysis and finite element analysis.
  • Mechanical Design of Mechanical Systems – Applies working knowledge of mechanical systems to develop sound design concepts that meet Cummins and customer requirements while considering product lifecycle and operating environments.
  • Mechanical Design Specification – Creates complete product specifications through solid models, configured engineering BOMs, and detailed drawings that communicate design intent for manufacturing and inspection.
  • Product Configuration and Change Management – Establishes and maintains product configuration baselines and manages the release, tracking, control, and communication of engineering changes throughout the product lifecycle.

Behavioral Competencies

  • Communicates Effectively – Communicates clearly and adapts communication to the needs of different audiences.
  • Decision Quality – Makes sound and timely decisions based on available technical information.
  • Drives Results – Consistently delivers assigned work while maintaining quality and schedule expectations.
  • Instills Trust – Builds confidence through honesty, integrity, accountability, and reliable execution.
  • Manages Complexity – Effectively evaluates complex and sometimes conflicting technical information to resolve issues.
  • Self-Development – Actively develops technical knowledge and capabilities through learning and feedback.
  • Values Differences – Recognizes and respects diverse perspectives and contributions.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma, certificate of completion of secondary education, or equivalent experience in an appropriate STEM field is required.
  • A regionally applicable certification or two-year Associate Degree from an accredited college or university in a relevant field may be required.
  • Relevant education or experience in Mechanical Engineering, Mechanical Design, CAD, Drafting, or a related STEM discipline is preferred.
  • Some work experience with intermediate-level technical knowledge gained through education, training, or on-the-job experience is required.
  • This position may require licensing or other requirements for compliance with export controls or sanctions regulations .

Skills & Experience

  • Experience in mechanical design, CAD modeling, drafting, or engineering documentation .
  • Working knowledge of Creo 3D modeling and drafting .
  • Ability to create and modify component and assembly models based on engineering requirements and design inputs.
  • Experience creating and revising engineering drawings with dimensions, tolerances, GD&T, notes, and material specifications .
  • Working knowledge of Windchill for CAD data, revisions, configuration, and product lifecycle management.
  • Understanding of engineering change management , including CR/CN/CA processes.
  • Working knowledge of mechanical components, assemblies, interfaces, manufacturing processes, and engineering standards.
  • Ability to perform detailed CAD self-checks and identify issues related to geometry, dimensions, interfaces, clearances, and drawing requirements.
  • Understanding of product configuration and change control principles.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to engineering documentation quality.
  • Ability to work effectively with engineers and cross-functional teams.
  • Ability to manage assigned work against quality and delivery expectations.
  • Ability to communicate risks, issues, and delays proactively.
  • Willingness to continuously develop technical and product knowledge through reviews, feedback, and hands-on experience.

job.title: Senior Analyst I, Environment Offer Data and Performance
job.description:
Job Description

Job Summary

As an Analyst – Environment Offer Data and Performance, you will collect, assess, analyze, and interpret environmental data related to products and solutions using recognized environmental assessment methodologies and frameworks such as LCA, PEP, and EPD.

You will support sustainable product development by identifying environmental improvement opportunities, ensuring environmental data accuracy and completeness in IT systems, and enabling compliance with environmental regulations and reporting standards.

The role contributes directly to the organization’s sustainability strategy, decarbonization objectives, circular economy initiatives, and environmentally responsible product innovation. You will collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to transform environmental data into actionable insights supporting sustainable decision-making and regulatory compliance.

You will independently solve routine and moderately complex technical challenges related to sustainability data, environmental compliance, and product environmental performance while working under general guidance and established organizational standards.

Key Responsibilities

  • Collect, validate, manage, and maintain environmental product data across internal systems and sustainability platforms.
  • Conduct environmental assessments using methodologies and frameworks such as LCA, PEP, and EPD.
  • Analyze environmental performance indicators and identify opportunities for sustainability improvement.
  • Support product sustainability initiatives including decarbonization, eco-design, material transparency, and circular economy programs.
  • Ensure environmental data quality, completeness, traceability, and governance across enterprise systems.
  • Support compliance with environmental regulations, customer requirements, and sustainability standards.
  • Collaborate with Offer Management, R&D, Sustainability, Procurement, Quality, and Digital teams.

You will get your hands dirty, troubleshooting application, network, database, and architectural challenges using a suite of internal AWS Cloud tools as well as your existing knowledge and toolkits. We are seeking individuals with strong backgrounds in I.T. Consulting and in any of these related areas such as Solution Designing, Application and System Development, Database Management, Big Data and Analytics, DevOps Consulting, and Media technologies. job.title: Software Engineering Manager, Google Home, SRE
job.description:
About the job

Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) combines software and systems engineering to build and run large-scale, massively distributed, fault-tolerant systems. SRE ensures that Google's services—both our internally critical and our externally-visible systems—have reliability, uptime appropriate to users' needs and a fast rate of improvement. Additionally SRE’s will keep an ever-watchful eye on our systems capacity and performance.

Much of our software development focuses on optimizing existing systems, building infrastructure and eliminating work through automation. On the SRE team, you’ll have the opportunity to manage the complex challenges of scale which are unique to Google, while using your expertise in coding, algorithms, complexity analysis and large-scale system design.

SRE's culture of intellectual curiosity, problem solving and openness is key to its success. Our organization brings together people with a wide variety of backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. We encourage them to collaborate, think big and take risks in a blame-free environment. We promote self-direction to work on meaningful projects, while we also strive to create an environment that provides the support and mentorship needed to learn and grow.

To learn more: check out our books on [Site Reliability Engineering](https://landing.google.com/sre/book.html) or read a [career profile](https://careers.google.com/stories/site-reliability-engineering-profile-google/) about why a Software Engineer chose to join SRE. Behind everything our users see online is the architecture built by the Technical Infrastructure team to keep it running. From developing and maintaining our data centers to building the next generation of Google platforms, we make Google's product portfolio possible. We're proud to be our engineers' engineers and love voiding warranties by taking things apart so we can rebuild them. We keep our networks up and running, ensuring our users have the best and fastest experience possible.

Responsibilities

  • Lead a team of Software/Systems Engineers on projects for users and be directly responsible for uptime.
  • Own end-to-end availability and performance of key services and build automation to prevent problem recurrence. Automate response to all non-exceptional service conditions.
  • Lead by example, mentor the team and establish credibility through quality technical execution.
  • Manage on-call rotations across continents, using a follow-the-sun model.
  • Design, write and deliver software to improve the availability, scalability, latency and efficiency of Google's services.

Information collected and processed as part of your Google Careers profile, and any job applications you choose to submit is subject to Google's [Applicant and Candidate Privacy Policy](./privacy-policy).

job.title: Senior Software Engineer, Cloud Networking (Mandarin, English)
job.description:
About the job

Google's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. Our products need to handle information at massive scale, and extend well beyond web search. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google’s needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward.

Interconnect has been one of the key features for GCP to onboard large enterprises and as such is a high impact project.

In this role, you will build Cloud Interconnect, which virtualizes the edge and foundation and allows enterprise customers to connect their on-premises data centers/networks to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) at 100 and 10 Gb/s speed. You will also span to connecting smaller customers through partners, as well as building ultra-low-latency interconnects in order for customers to be able to use large file stores and databases operated by third-parties, adjacent to Google data centers. You will manage complexity from physical network and routers through cloud virtualization.**

Responsibilities

  • Support the launch of Cloud networking infrastructure to enable Artificial Intelligence (AI)-motivated workloads to unlock their full potential.
  • Design, develop, and scale cloud networking products and infrastructure to enable the hybrid cloud technical roadmap, ensure their availability, reliability, and performance.
  • Advocate and drive engineering and operational excellence.
  • Create designs for complex projects, collaborate with cross-functional teams to deliver on ambitious goals.

Information collected and processed as part of your Google Careers profile, and any job applications you choose to submit is subject to Google's [Applicant and Candidate Privacy Policy](./privacy-policy).

job.title: Senior Staff Tech Lead Manager, TPU Workload Onboarding and Optimization
job.description:
About the job

Like Google's own ambitions, the work of a Software Engineer goes beyond just Search. Software Engineering Managers have not only the technical expertise to take on and provide technical leadership to major projects, but also manage a team of Engineers. You not only optimize your own code but make sure Engineers are able to optimize theirs. As a Software Engineering Manager you manage your project goals, contribute to product strategy and help develop your team. Teams work all across the company, in areas such as information retrieval, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking, security, data compression, user interface design; the list goes on and is growing every day. Operating with scale and speed, our exceptional software engineers are just getting started -- and as a manager, you guide the way.

With technical and leadership expertise, you manage engineers across multiple teams and locations, a large product budget and oversee the deployment of large-scale projects across multiple sites internationally.

Our mission is to provide the best possible cloud-based ML pre-training, post-training, and inference solutions to our customers. The team is part of the AI Engine and focuses on the training/inference workloads and the infrastructure. Our team’s mission is to provide the infrastructure and the framework support to enable serving of ML models on Cloud GPUs and TPUs. In particular, we support external customers for their ML training/inference onboarding and optimizations. You will join a team working on an emergent product with potential to change how customers use Google infrastructure for machine learning training/inference. It is a dynamic and exciting environment that is open to change and is full of growth opportunities.

The AI and Infrastructure team is redefining what’s possible. We empower Google customers with breakthrough capabilities and insights by delivering AI and Infrastructure at unparalleled scale, efficiency, reliability and velocity. Our customers include Googlers, Google Cloud customers, and billions of Google users worldwide.

We're the driving force behind Google's groundbreaking innovations, empowering the development of our cutting-edge AI models, delivering unparalleled computing power to global services, and providing the essential platforms that enable developers to build the future. From software to hardware our teams are shaping the future of world-leading hyperscale computing, with key teams working on the development of our TPUs, Vertex AI for Google Cloud, Google Global Networking, Data Center operations, systems research, and much more.

Responsibilities

  • Act as a Senior Software Manager leading the onboarding for stable stack, and optimization for training and serving solutions on the latest TPU NPIs. Set the technical direction and architect the training/inference serving onboarding and optimization frameworks for our customer needs.
  • Collaborate with the ML research, ML performance, model optimization tooling, and other optimization teams.
  • Ship stable stack to our customers for training/inference optimization solutions on TPU.

job.title: Project Manager - Data Centre Build
job.description:
Firmus Technologies

Firmus Technologies is a global leader pioneering the development and operation of efficient AI infrastructure across Asia Pacific.

Founded in Australia in 2019, our mission is to create the most efficient AI infrastructure by combining cutting-edge technology with a steadfast commitment to sustainability.

At Firmus, we are unique in our approach. We design, build, and operate a new class of digital infrastructure – the AI Factory. Through our model-to-grid technology approach, we have pushed the boundaries of multi-generational liquid cooling systems, energy management, AI software orchestration, and construction. For our customers, this approach allows us to make every watt count and deliver low-cost AI tokens globally.

Firmus AI Cloud

Our large-scale GPU cloud platform, Firmus AI Cloud, is purpose-built to deliver energy-efficient AI compute at scale to customers.

It empowers developers, enterprises, educational institutions, and government users to train and deploy AI models with unmatched efficiency and cost savings. With an ever-growing suite of services and applications, we are committed to delivering a cloud experience that is market-leading, proprietary, and built to scale.

Why Firmus?

As an NVIDIA Cloud and Engineering partner in Asia Pacific, you will gain skills, experience, and exposure across the AI industry and be part of shaping what this industry looks like for decades to come.

We are founder-led, not a big corporate. Decisions happen fast, our leaders are accessible, and there's minimum bureaucracy between you and the work. Ownership comes early. Whatever your role, you will have a direct line to outcomes, helping shape how the business grows as we scale nationally across a long-term, large-scale roadmap.

Work alongside founders and experts in AI infrastructure, energy systems and next-generation compute.

What we build here has impact beyond the business. Our AI Factories are designed to operate as assets to the energy grid to actively strengthen the communities and regions they operate in rather than drawing from them.

Considering applying? You don't need a perfect background to join our team. If you're driven and curious, there's a path for you. We back our people to grow into new domains and take on challenges beyond their previous experience.

Role Summary

The Project Manager – Capital Projects (Tailem Bend) is responsible for the delivery of the Tailem Bend project within Firmus’ South Australian capital projects portfolio. The role is responsible for the project end to end — from initial project gateway approval through to handover to the operations team — and for delivering it in line with the approved scope, budget, programme, quality and safety requirements.

The role reports to the Senior Project Manager – Capital Projects (South Australia), who holds single-point accountability for the region. Design, cost and schedule changes are identified, assessed and recommended by this role, and authorised by the Senior Project Manager. The Project Manager is responsible for ensuring no change proceeds without that authorisation, and that approved changes are implemented, recorded and reflected in the project cost report and programme.

Day to day, the role runs the project on the ground — directing consultants, contractors and vendors, controlling the programme and cost, maintaining safety and quality standards, and coordinating the planning, design, procurement, construction, fit-out, commissioning and deployment activities required to hand over a complete and operable facility. The role sits within the Capital Projects Team, which forms part of the Development Division under the Chief Development Officer.

Key Responsibilities

Project Delivery

  • Deliver the Tailem Bend project from initial project gateway approval through to handover to the operations team, in line with the approved scope, budget, programme, quality and safety requirements.
  • Manage each phase of the project — feasibility, approvals, design development, procurement, construction, fit-out, commissioning and deployment — and keep the sequence and interfaces between them under control.
  • Prepare the project material required for gateway and investment approvals, including scope, cost plan, programme and risk, for review by the Senior Project Manager – Capital Projects.
  • Progress planning approvals, authority conditions, utility and network connections and enabling works in line with the approved programme.
  • Run the day-to-day site delivery, including site supervision, coordination of trades and resolution of on-site issues.

Programme and Cost Control

  • Own and maintain the project programme, protecting critical path, interface dates and key milestones.
  • Manage the project budget, including commitments, invoicing, variations, contingency drawdown and forecast to completion, with support from project controls.
  • Produce accurate, timely project reporting on progress, cost, risk, safety and readiness for the Senior Project Manager – Capital Projects.
  • Identify risks, delays and cost exposures early, propose mitigation, and escalate promptly rather than after impact.
  • Maintain complete and current project records, registers and documentation throughout delivery.

Design and Change Management

  • Coordinate design development with consultants to ensure the design meets the approved brief, is buildable and is delivered to cost and programme.
  • Identify, assess and document every design, cost and schedule change, including its scope, cost, programme and risk impact.
  • Submit all changes to the Senior Project Manager – Capital Projects for authorisation — no change is to proceed on site without it.
  • Implement approved changes and ensure they are reflected in the drawings, cost report, programme and project records.
  • Manage requests for information, technical queries and design clarifications through to closure.

Procurement, Consultants and Contractors

  • Support procurement strategy and packaging for the project with the supply chain and procurement functions, including long-lead equipment and specialist trades.
  • Manage the day-to-day performance of consultants, head contractors, construction managers, subcontractors and vendors engaged on the project.
  • Administer contracts, including scope definition, variations, claims, progress claims and payment recommendations, close-out and final account.
  • Hold delivery partners to the project programme and to the required cost, quality and safety standards.

Safety, Quality and Compliance

  • Ensure work health and safety requirements are understood and met by all parties on site, and that safety performance is actively managed rather than assumed.
  • Ensure the works are delivered to the specified quality standards, with inspection and test plans, hold points and defect management applied.
  • Ensure compliance with permit and approval conditions, environmental requirements and applicable codes and standards.
  • Report incidents, near misses and non-conformances promptly and see corrective actions through to closure.

Stakeholder and Authority Engagement

  • Act as the Firmus representative on site, maintaining working relationships with the council, planning authority, network and utility providers, neighbours and the local community.
  • Coordinate with internal functions — development and planning, design and engineering, project controls, energy and operations — to keep project delivery aligned with business requirements.
  • Support the Senior Project Manager in customer engagement relating to the project through delivery, commissioning and handover.

Commissioning, Deployment and Handover

  • Coordinate commissioning, acceptance testing and witnessing through to a complete and operable facility.
  • Confirm site readiness, environmental conditions and access ahead of equipment delivery, installation and deployment.
  • Meet the handover readiness criteria set for the region, covering safety, quality, testing and documentation.
  • Compile and transfer handover documentation — as-builts, O&M manuals, warranties, asset registers, spares and operator training.
  • Manage defects, close-out and the transition of responsibility to the operations team.

Skills & Experience

Required Skills

  • Tertiary qualification in Engineering, Construction, Project Management or a related technical discipline
  • 6+ years’ experience delivering capital projects, ideally in data centres, mission-critical, energy or industrial infrastructure
  • Demonstrated experience running a project on site from design and procurement through construction and commissioning to handover
  • Strong programme and cost control, including scheduling, cost tracking, forecasting, variations and change control
  • Sound contract administration capability across construction management, design and construct, or traditional delivery models
  • Practical working knowledge of work health and safety obligations and quality management on an active construction site
  • Experience coordinating consultants, head contractors, subcontractors and vendors to a single programme
  • Experience with planning approvals, authority conditions and utility or network connections
  • Clear written and verbal communication, including concise project reporting to senior leadership
  • Familiarity with high-density compute environments and liquid or immersion cooling systems advantageous
  • Based in, or willing to relocate to, Adelaide or Tailem Bend, with regular travel to site
  • PMP, PRINCE2 or equivalent project management certification advantageous

Success Metrics

  • The Tailem Bend project progresses from gateway approval to handover on time, on budget and to the required quality and safety standards.
  • Project reporting is accurate, timely and trusted, giving the Senior Project Manager a reliable view of cost, programme, risk and readiness at all times.
  • Design, cost and schedule changes are identified early, properly assessed, authorised before they proceed, and reflected in the cost report and programme.
  • Risks, delays and cost exposures are escalated ahead of impact, with practical mitigation proposed rather than problems simply reported.
  • Safety and quality standards are met on site, with incidents, non-conformances and defects managed through to closure.
  • Consultants, contractors and vendors perform to programme, cost and quality, with contracts properly administered and closed out.

job.description:
Manager, Controllership - Financial Shared Services

Johnson Controls is looking for a finance leader to oversee a key function within our financial shared services organization in a business center. This role supports accurate accounting operations, strong controls, and timely financial information that helps the business make sound decisions.

Role Overview

You will lead a specific accounting function with responsibility for daily, weekly, and monthly activities, team coordination, and the quality of financial output. The role is suited to an experienced accounting professional who can balance operational execution, control discipline, and people leadership in a shared services environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan and manage the day-to-day, weekly, and monthly accounting activities for the assigned function.
  • Establish and maintain accounting systems, procedures, and controls that support accurate financial information.
  • Review reconciliations, journal entries, and related accounting outputs to help ensure completeness and accuracy.
  • Lead, coach, and develop team members responsible for the function.
  • Partner with internal finance stakeholders and the broader business center to support service delivery and issue resolution.
  • Monitor workflow, priorities, and deadlines to keep accounting activities on track.
  • Support audit, compliance, and control requirements as part of the shared services operating model.
  • Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, consistency, and standardization across the function.

How You Will Do It

  • Own the function with accountability for accuracy, timeliness, and follow-through.
  • Stay close to the work by understanding daily execution, resolving obstacles quickly, and supporting your team where needed.
  • Use clear controls and disciplined reviews to protect the integrity of financial information.
  • Look for practical ways to improve processes, reduce rework, and strengthen consistency.
  • Work as one team by building trust with finance partners, sharing knowledge, and coaching for performance.

Qualifications

  • University degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • At least 8 years of progressive experience in accounting, controllership, or financial shared services.
  • Experience leading or managing a team in a finance or accounting environment.
  • Strong knowledge of accounting processes, reconciliations, journal entries, controls, and close activities.
  • Ability to establish accounting systems and processes that support accurate and reliable reporting.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Experience working in a shared services, business center, or similar high-volume finance environment.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining quality and deadlines.

Nice to Have

  • Experience driving process improvement or standardization initiatives in finance operations.
  • Background supporting internal or external audits.
  • Experience in a global or multi-site accounting environment.

Why Join Us

This is an opportunity to lead an important finance function where your work directly supports accuracy, control, and service quality. At Johnson Controls, you will work with a collaborative team environment and have the chance to help strengthen shared services processes while developing the people around you.

If you are ready to lead with accountability and help improve the finance function, we encourage you to apply.

Job Summary

We are seeking a skilled Manager Treasury Support to join Treasury Operations Tower– -Global Finance Services Division .

The Corporate Treasury team is looking for a talented and motivated Regional Operations Lead on the Treasury Services Tower team. The position is tasked with activities that include but are not limited to the leadership of treasury processes and projects in the U.S and Mexico, and support of the treasury budget and SOX processes, and the Inventory 180 dealer financing program.

The preference for this role is to be based out of Whitefield, Bangalore -KA

What you will do

  • Manages the delivery of treasury processes and projects in the U.S. and Mexico
  • Manages a team in Mexico supporting the delivery of treasury processes and services
  • Supports the Global Business Services transformation initiative and works with the Treasury Global Operations Lead to develop and implement global strategies for enhancing treasury processes and procedures
  • Serves as the Internal Control Coordinator (ICC) for the global Treasury team. Lead audit coordination and execution: Audits – IAAS / Deloitte, SOX Audits, ad-hoc audit requests, liaison with SOX team. This support will include training, review of documentation, testing, and remediation plans
  • Lead budget coordinator for the global Treasury team. Develop deep expertise of Treasury’s controllable costs. Analyze the budget results and provide business insights to the global Treasury team. Serve as the liaison between Treasury and Accounting for the budget process. Prepare monthly budget reporting and analysis
  • Supports Inventory 180 Treasury process owner in managing the dealer financing program in collaboration with dealers and insurers.
  • Manages the country exposure reporting process. Prepare country exposure reports for management on a quarterly basis
  • Leads continuous improvement projects for the Treasury Services Tower to simplify and standardize the processes under management. Implement best in class reporting processes through standardization, automation and a streamlined reporting structure

What you will have

  • Education/Experience: college or university degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or other business-related fields; 8+ years of job-related experience in Treasury / Finance
  • Planning: Tactical, Strategic:Knowledge of effective planning techniques and ability to contribute to operational (short term), tactical (1-2 years) and strategic (3-5 years) planning in support of the overall business plan

job.title: Human Resources Intern (Credit Bearing)
job.description:
Job Description

Your Work Shapes the World at Caterpillar Inc.

When you join Caterpillar, you're joining a global team who cares not just about the work we do – but also about each other. We are the makers, problem solvers, and future world builders who are creating stronger, more sustainable communities. We don't just talk about progress and innovation here – we make it happen, with our customers, where we work and live. Together, we are building a better world, so we can all enjoy living in it.

We are looking for an enthusiastic and driven Human Resources (HR) Intern to assist our Regional HR department with HR-related activities. You will handle and manage all aspects of the employee life cycle in our company and with the opportunity to possibly engage with senior leaders in the Asia Pacific region.

To be successful as an HR Intern, you should keep abreast of the latest developments in labor legislation to determine how company HR policies may be affected. Ultimately, an outstanding HR Intern should be detail-oriented and able to demonstrate excellent administrative and organizational skills.

What You Will Do

  • Assist to review job descriptions with leaders and posting in various platforms
  • Understand how to screen candidates and coordination of interviews including package negotiation
  • Conduct review of internal HR policies and procedures to make recommendations
  • Review insurance (life /medical) policies and make recommendations
  • Assist to create marketing/digital content (newsletter / infographics / short videos)
  • Prepare HR-related reports as needed, e.g. training budgets by department
  • Address employee queries about benefits (like benefits eligibility)
  • Organise virtual training/ networking events
  • Creative brainstorming
  • Handle necessary administrative work
  • Develop marketing of materials/campaigns for social media platforms and events
  • Resume screening and coordination of interviews
  • Activity management and planning for training activities

What You Have

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resource Management or studying toward a degree in Human Resource Management or related field.
  • Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and take ownership of assigned responsibilities.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Tech-savvy, open-minded, and results-oriented with a willingness to embrace new ideas and technologies.
  • Eager to learn, adaptable, and proactive in seeking growth opportunities.
  • Creative thinker with the ability to generate innovative ideas and contribute fresh perspectives.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with diverse stakeholders.

Learning Outcomes

  • Understanding of Financial business model in a captive environment
  • Acquire working knowledge of Labour Regulations in AP countries
  • Develop communication skills (verbal and writing) and creativity for regional HR newsletter
  • Learn the practical know-hows of Total Rewards analysis, writing HR policies, investigation processes, etc
  • Practical application of Microsoft Office tools to enhance working processes
  • Build long-lasting relationships with the HR regional teams and other employees

Additional Information

  • Internship must be a credit-bearing requirement as part of the candidate's academic program.
  • This position requires the intern to be onsite five days per week.
  • Candidates should be available for a minimum six-month internship, to maximize learning and exposure opportunities.
  • Caterpillar is not currently hiring individuals for this position who now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status; however, as a global company, Caterpillar offers many job opportunities outside of Singapore which can be found through our employment website at www.caterpillar.com/careers.

How We Support You (Internship Benefits)

Our goal at Caterpillar is for you to have a rewarding internship. Besides a monthly stipend, additional benefits include paid annual leave (pro-rated based on internship period), medical leave, in-house cafeteria and transportation to and from Boon Lay MRT station.

About Caterpillar

Caterpillar Inc. is the world’s leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, off-highway diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines and diesel-electric locomotives. For nearly 100 years, we’ve been helping customers build a better, more sustainable world and are committed and contributing to a reduced-carbon future. Our innovative products and services, backed by our global dealer network, provide exceptional value that helps customers succeed.

This position requires working onsite five days a week.Visa Sponsorship is not available for this position. Posting Dates:

October 16, 2026 - November 14, 2026 Caterpillar is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants of any age are encouraged to apply
